skill.name: agentdb-performance-optimization
skill.description: Optimize AgentDB vector database performance with quantization, HNSW indexing, caching, batching, and monitoring guidance.
skill.summary: Tune AgentDB vector databases for faster search, lower memory use, and better scaling.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, TypeScript examples, documentation links, and illustrative local database paths. Three bash examples instruct users to run unpinned npx commands, which creates a moderate supply-chain risk if users copy them without verifying the package.

remediation.suggestion: Replace agentdb@latest with a reviewed fixed version and tell users to verify the npm package before running benchmark or stats commands.
Add a short warning before shell commands that explains they execute local tools and should only be run in trusted projects.

content.value_statement: Large AgentDB vector stores can become slow and memory intensive. This skill gives practical tuning steps for search speed, memory use, and scaling.
actual_capabilities: Explains binary, scalar, product, and full precision quantization tradeoffs.
Shows how to configure HNSW parameters for speed, recall, and memory.
Provides cache sizing guidance for small, medium, and large applications.
Describes batch insert and parallel retrieval patterns for vector workloads.
Includes monitoring commands and metrics for AgentDB performance checks.
Maps optimization recipes to speed, accuracy, memory, and scale goals.
limitations: Requires an existing AgentDB or agentic-flow application.
Performance claims depend on hardware, dataset shape, and embedding size.
Does not validate package versions or execute benchmarks for the user.
Some examples may need adaptation for current AgentDB APIs.

use_cases.title: Reduce Vector Search Latency
use_cases.description: Tune HNSW search parameters and cache settings for faster retrieval in production applications.

use_cases.title: Lower Memory Costs
use_cases.description: Choose a quantization strategy that reduces storage while preserving acceptable search quality.

use_cases.title: Plan Large Dataset Scaling
use_cases.description: Select indexing, batching, and monitoring patterns before growing to hundreds of thousands of vectors.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Basic Optimization
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to recommend AgentDB settings for a small vector store with less than 10,000 vectors and high accuracy needs.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Memory Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare binary, scalar, and product quantization for my AgentDB dataset, including memory savings and accuracy tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Search Latency
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to tune HNSW parameters, cache size, and retrieval settings for an AgentDB workload with 500,000 vectors.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Scaling Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create an AgentDB scaling plan for one million vectors, including batching, monitoring metrics, and rollback risks.

output_examples.input: I have 100,000 vectors and search is slow.
output_examples.output: A concise tuning plan that recommends scalar quantization, HNSW parameter checks, cache sizing, and latency measurements before and after changes.

output_examples.input: I need the smallest memory footprint for an edge deployment.
output_examples.output: A tradeoff summary that favors binary quantization, a small cache, reduced HNSW connections, and an accuracy validation step.

output_examples.input: I want to monitor AgentDB performance in production.
output_examples.output: A checklist of metrics such as database size, cache hit rate, total patterns, average confidence, and search latency.

best_practices: Benchmark before and after each optimization so changes have measurable value.
Choose quantization based on recall requirements, not memory savings alone.
Pin and verify command-line tools before running benchmark or stats commands.
anti_patterns: Using binary quantization for accuracy-critical workloads without recall testing.
Increasing HNSW quality settings without measuring memory and build time impact.
Running unpinned package commands from documentation in sensitive projects.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize?
faq.answer: It focuses on AgentDB vector search speed, memory use, indexing, caching, batching, and monitoring.

faq.question: Does it execute benchmark commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and guidance, but users decide whether to run commands.

faq.question: Which quantization option is safest for accuracy?
faq.answer: Full precision preserves accuracy, while scalar quantization is usually the balanced compressed option.

faq.question: Can it help with very large vector stores?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for datasets from small stores to more than one million vectors.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude?
faq.answer: No. The skill is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should I verify before using the shell examples?
faq.answer: Verify the package source, pin a trusted version, and run commands only in a trusted project.
